tool.name: mirtop counts
tool.description: count table of miRNAs and isomiRs from mirGFF3
tool.command: ln -s '$gff' input.gff && mkdir output && @STAGE_ANNOTATION@ mirtop counts --gff input.gff --hairpin hairpin.fa --gtf annotation.gff3 --sps '$sps' $add_extra -o output ## mirtop writes all sample columns as one tab-joined field, which pandas then quotes as CSV; ## parse that quoting properly so quotes inside sample names survive && python -c 'import csv, sys; [sys.stdout.write("\t".join(row) + "\n") for row in csv.reader(open(sys.argv[1]), delimiter="\t")]' output/input.tsv > '$output'

param.label: Add nucleotide-level variant columns
param.help: Adds iso_5p_nt, iso_3p_nt, iso_add3p_nt and iso_snp_nt columns. nf-core/smrnaseq turns this on.

tool.help:
## What it does
Converts a mirGFF3 file, as written by **mirtop gff**, into a tab-separated count table with one row per unique read sequence and one column per sample.
Give it the same hairpin FASTA, miRNA annotation and species code that were used to make the mirGFF3 file. mirtop always reads the annotation, because it works out the database (miRBase or MirGeneDB) from the annotation's header lines, and stops with an error if it cannot. The hairpins are only used for the nucleotide-level columns.
## Output columns
- `UID`: the sequence-derived read identifier - `Read`: the read sequence - `miRNA`: the mature miRNA the read was assigned to - `Variant`: isomiR variant types, or `NA` for the reference miRNA - `iso_5p`, `iso_3p`, `iso_add3p`, `iso_snp`: size of each variant - `iso_5p_nt`, `iso_3p_nt`, `iso_add3p_nt`, `iso_snp_nt`: the nucleotides involved (only with *Add nucleotide-level variant columns* on) - one count column per sample
To get counts per mature miRNA, sum the sample columns by `miRNA`.
When nucleotide-level columns are requested, reads whose precursor or mature miRNA is missing from the hairpin FASTA or annotation are left out of the table.
